safest_first_batch.label: B01-github-tracking-settings
safest_first_batch.rationale: Both rows are deterministic value-policy helpers with no clocks, stores, network, UI, or process-global state; the current GitHub connector eval already reaches the owning production type.

rows.rationale: The 120-second bound and synthesis call are hardwired inside the scheduler; deterministic timeout/degraded-marker coverage needs an injected clock or bounded-turn seam and an observability decision.
The loop owns ContinuousClock sleeps, focus/streaming state, and private restart behavior; honest timing and cancellation coverage needs a clock/sleeper or lifecycle seam.
runDueJobs already accepts isolated execution dependencies and a temporary data root, so a test can execute each due-job outcome and assert the production activity JSONL receipt.
Coordinator entry points and the ContextSourceRegistrationRefreshing mirror-provider protocol already allow a fake provider to execute discovery refresh without a new production seam.
The reconciliation method is directly callable against a temporary DeskStore and can assert parent/child status and alias stability with no new boundary.
The authenticated-login equality policy is a deterministic production helper that can be called with synthetic settings and login values.
The default and 1...2160 clamp are deterministic production value semantics directly executable without storage or network setup.
The current KnowledgeGraphView filters synchronously and has no debounce behavior; coverage requires deciding whether to add debounce or retire/rename the row.
The operation reads NSUbiquitousKeyValueStore.default and writes Keychain-backed pairing state directly; executing it hermetically needs KVS and credential-store seams.
The Node helper already accepts a temporary bridge directory and explicit job/by arguments, so success and malformed-job behavior can be executed directly.
A temporary ContextSQLiteStore can execute production insert/delete paths and then query the real FTS5 table to prove write/read synchronization.
